seoTitle: How to Use Appointment Reports in GoHighLevel
metaDescription: Find the Appointment report in GoHighLevel's Reporting section, set a date range, and read the booking, no-show, channel, and top-calendar breakdowns.
intro: Appointment reports in GoHighLevel give a clear picture of how scheduling is performing, from bookings to cancellations to no-shows, once you know where the report lives and how its date range works. This guide walks through the Reporting section's layout, the Appointment report tab, and the breakdown panels underneath the headline metrics, including a couple of panels easy to miss on a first look. It's built for small business owners and marketers who want appointment data to inform decisions instead of sitting unused in a tab they never open.

steps.heading: Open the Reporting section
steps.body: Reporting sits in the left sidebar below Memberships and Media Storage. Landing here defaults to the Custom reports tab, which shows an overview panel explaining what the reporting tools do: build multi-page reports, share them automatically, and turn data into insights, plus a New report button. Along the top, a row of tabs breaks reporting into specific areas: Custom reports, Google Ads, Meta Ads (Facebook Ads) report, Attribution report, Call report, Appointment report, and Local Marketing Audit.

image.caption: The Reporting section's overview, with tabs across the top for each report type including Appointment report.

steps.heading: Click into Appointment report and set your date range
steps.body: Selecting Appointment report opens a page headed "Appointment reporting" with a date range field near the top left, defaulted to a recent window. Clicking it opens a two-month calendar picker with quick presets: This week, Last week, Last 7 days, This month, This year, alongside manual date selection and a Confirm button to lock in the range. A dropdown next to it, All calendars, lets you scope the report to a single calendar instead of every booking source combined.

image.caption: The date range picker open on the Appointment reporting page, with quick presets like This week and Last 7 days alongside manual calendar selection.

steps.heading: Read the metrics tiles across the top
steps.body: Once a range is set, a row of tiles summarizes the period at a glance: Booked, Confirmed, Cancelled, New, Showed, No-show, Invalid, and Rescheduled, each showing a raw count. On a fresh account or a quiet date range these all read zero, but on an active calendar this row is the fastest way to spot a problem. A high No-show count relative to Showed is the clearest signal that reminder timing or confirmation messaging needs attention.

image.caption: The Appointment reporting metrics row, showing Booked, Confirmed, Cancelled, No-show, and other counts for the selected date range.

steps.heading: Break the numbers down by Channel, Source, and top performers
steps.body:
Below the tiles, Channel and Source panels (the latter filterable by Funnel) show where appointments are coming from: which booking channel or marketing source is driving bookings and which ones are underperforming. GoHighLevel's own documentation notes that the Channel breakdown includes an Event Sync category, covering appointments pulled in from a connected Google, Outlook, iCloud, or Calendly calendar instead of being booked through a GoHighLevel funnel directly, so don't be surprised to see it sitting alongside your marketing channels.

Further down, a Top Performing Calendars panel and a Top 5 Users by Number of Appointments panel rank volume by calendar and by team member, a Most Popular Days panel shows which weekdays draw the most bookings, and a dedicated panel surfaces the calendars with the highest cancellation and reschedule counts. Together these are the layer that turns a raw appointment count into something actionable: a specific funnel generating bookings that don't show up tells you to fix that funnel's confirmation flow, not your calendar in general.

steps.heading: Check Outcomes, then make the report a habit
steps.body: An Outcomes panel groups what ultimately happened to each appointment, rounding out the page below the channel and calendar breakdowns. On its own, though, the report only helps if it's opened more than once. Set a recurring reminder, weekly is reasonable for most service businesses, to revisit the Appointment report tab, adjust the date range to the prior period, and scan the metrics row and the cancellation panel for anything that shifted. Catching a rising No-show count or an underperforming channel early is far cheaper than finding it a quarter later in a broader revenue review.

faq.question: Where is the Appointment report in GoHighLevel?
faq.answer: Go to Reporting in the left sidebar, then click the Appointment report tab in the row of report types across the top, next to Call report and Local Marketing Audit.

faq.question: What does an appointment report in GoHighLevel show?
faq.answer: A metrics row covering Booked, Confirmed, Cancelled, New, Showed, No-show, Invalid, and Rescheduled counts for your chosen date range, plus breakdowns by Channel, Source, Outcomes, top calendars, top users, most popular booking days, and calendars with the most cancellations or reschedules.

faq.question: What is an Event Sync appointment in the Channel breakdown?
faq.answer: According to GoHighLevel's own support documentation, Event Sync covers appointments with at least one attendee that came in through a calendar connected from Google, Outlook, iCloud, or Calendly, not through a GoHighLevel booking funnel. It shows up as its own slice in the Channel panel.

faq.question: Can I filter the report to a specific calendar?
faq.answer: Yes. The All calendars dropdown next to the date range lets you scope the report to one calendar instead of combining every booking source, useful once the top-calendar panels show you have several active.

faq.question: Can I export or print the report?
faq.answer: GoHighLevel's documentation references a print option on the report page. It doesn't detail a broader spreadsheet export for this specific report, so treat print, or GoHighLevel's separate custom-reports builder, as your options instead of assuming a one-click CSV export exists here.

faq.question: How can appointment reports help reduce no-shows?
faq.answer: Watching the No-show tile against Showed over successive date ranges helps catch a rising trend early, so reminder timing or confirmation messaging can be adjusted before it becomes a bigger revenue problem.
